ADR-0024 — the plugin runs behind our endpoints.
It is never in front of the browser: better-auth's device-authorization routes are
calls reach it. Two findings force this: `/device/token` returns a
Bearer token in JSON and never sets a cookie (ADR-0008/0012 forbid

code for the caller's account while the origin check skips all GETs
Same shape as the UserContextGuard seam: better-auth is the
mechanism, our API owns the surface.
ADR-0023 — the router lives here and only here.
prop-driven: a screen never imports `@react-navigation/*`, never
calls a navigation hook, never imports a navigation type. That
constraint is what keeps the 14 prop-mounted test files untouched
(blast radius 1, not 15) — and it is enforced at review, not hoped for.

All /v1 access is scoped by the trusted userId the UserContextGuard
establishes (ADR-0007/0012) — a verified better-auth session or an
HMAC-signed guest cookie, never a client-supplied identity.
better-auth (ADR-0009) mounts *behind* that seam, not around it.
